---
title: "The brain region hierarchy"
---

Brain regions in the IBL atlas form a tree, and each region has more than one identifier. This
page explains the tree, the identifiers and how they encode the hemisphere.

## Regions form a tree

Every region has a parent, up to `root`. Primary motor area, `MOp`, sits inside `MO`, inside
`Isocortex`, and so on up the tree:

`root` → `grey` → `CH` → `CTX` → `CTXpl` → `Isocortex` → `MO` → `MOp`

The tree has 11 levels, from `root` at level 0 to the finest regions at level 10. You can browse
it in the
[Allen Brain Atlas viewer](https://atlas.brain-map.org/atlas?atlas=602630314#atlas=602630314&plate=576989940&structure=549&x=5280.261048274253&y=3744.2747201492534&zoom=-3&resolution=11.93&z=3).

A point in `MOp` is also in `Isocortex` and in `grey`. Describing a region more coarsely means
choosing a higher level of the tree, which is what the
[brain region mappings](brain-region-mappings.qmd) do.

## Three identifiers

| Identifier | Example for primary motor area | What it is |
|---|---|---|
| **Acronym** | `MOp` | Short human-readable label |
| **Allen id** | `985` | The Allen Institute's region id |
| **Index** | `19` | Position of the region in the atlas's table of regions |

The acronym and the Allen id identify the region itself. The index is a position in the table
of regions, and it is what the atlas label volume stores for each voxel.

## The sign of the id gives the hemisphere

The table of regions holds every region twice, once for each hemisphere. Both entries share the
same acronym; the right-hemisphere entry has a positive Allen id and the left-hemisphere entry
has the negated id. `MOp` on the right is `985`, and `MOp` on the left is `-985`.

With the `void` entry, id `0`, for space outside the brain, the table has 2655 entries: 1327
regions per hemisphere.

## Next

The hierarchy is the basis of the mappings, and the hemisphere sign is what lets a mapping
treat the two sides separately — see [Brain region mappings](brain-region-mappings.qmd).
